messages:
maria: quick follow-up from the quant-attn RFC thread — I sketched a potential fault we didn’t discuss: dequant-fusion ordering vs KV-cache layout. if we fuse dequant into attn kernel, where do we apply prefix/KV-copy shortcuts without extra mem?

ashwin: yeah been thinking about that. two competing constraints: 1) fused dequant avoids extra memcpy and improves perf for long sequences, 2) fused path complicates incremental kv updates and means kernels must understand our KV slab layout.

kevin: my worry: fused path could inflate peak memory because we need both quantized and dequant buffer live if fallback hits mid-seq. e.g., failure path -> we need to materialize dequant for all cached steps.

lina: can we do a lazy-materialize approach? keep quantized cache, and only dequant the slice needed for current attention window on demand. that keeps peak lower but adds branch overhead.

ashwin: lazy dequant sounds promising. practical idea: have kernel expose two entrypoints in registry: "attn_fused_dequant" (fast path) and "attn_dequant_on_demand" (fallback/lazy). scheduler picks based on runtime hints (seq_len, cache_hit_rate, available_mem).

maria: that matches my thinking. also need to define failure semantics: if fast path starts and then backend reason forces fallback (OOM, kernel not available), we need deterministic fallback that preserves kv positions.

kevin: implementation detail: avoid duplicating kv layout logic across runtime and kernels. propose a small KV adapter interface (C ABI) kernels can call to pull slices. runtime implements adapter for our slab layout. keeps kernel simple.

ashwin: +1. adapter surface should be tiny: get_slice(ptr, start, length, dest_ptr) and maybe prefetch hints. allows both fused and non-fused kernels to use same kv semantics.

lina: test plan thoughts: microbench for short/long seq, cache-miss vs cache-hit, and regression tests on memory watermark. also fuzz for fallback mid-window. can we add a test harness that simulates partial failures?

sam: for rollout, canary the fused path behind a feature flag per-customer. we should instrument metrics: per-token p95 latency, peak_rss, kernel_fallback_rate, and correctness diffs (logprobs or token mismatch) for regression alerting.

ashwin: about quant formats — FP8/INT8/INT4 all have different dequant cost. we should let kernel registry carry a "quant_profile" attribute so scheduler matches model->kernel combos. e.g., model.quant_profile = [Q4, Q8] and kernel advertises compat.

maria: agree. also need a graceful downgrade: if FP8 fused kernel is absent, route to INT8 dequant + higher precision fallback, with controlled quality warning in logs.

kevin: code snippet for kernel registration prototype:
```
REGISTER_KERNEL("attn_fused_dequant", {
  quant_profile: ["fp8-e4m3", "int8"],
  kv_adapter: true,
  shape_contract: "supports_dynamic_seqlen"
});
```

lina: nice. shape_contract will be key to avoid OOB on partial caches. also add a "max_extra_mem" field so scheduler can avoid kernels that exceed budget.

maria: ops-level compatibility: runtime must guarantee same random seeds for dropout paths and deterministic kv offsets. add an opt-in deterministic mode for canary runs.

sam: ops-level note: we should also add a fallback metric for "fallback_reason" labels (OOM, unsupported_quant, kernel_error) to speed triage.

ci-bot: build: bazel //eng/runtime/kernels:quant_attn_fused PASSED (tested fp8,int8).

maria: thanks ci-bot. next steps: ashwin to draft Registry API PR, kevin to prototype KV adapter shim, lina to add harness scenarios, sam to outline canary/alert playbook. i'll own the RFC follow-up doc.

ashwin: i'll start the PR today, will ping for design review.

kevin: will have prototype by EOW.

lina: adding test matrix to test infra now.

sam: will write the rollout checklist and metrics dashboard template.

maria: cool. meeting if needed but let’s keep async. thanks all :thumbsup:
